references.text: Here a similar situation is described where Jesus cannot be seized because his hour has not yet come, confirming that his life is under divine control until the appointed moment.
Jesus confirms that the hour he spoke of earlier has now arrived, and that his death is the appointed time for his glory, which was hidden earlier in chapter 7.
The text emphasizes that Jesus knew his hour had come to depart from this world, a direct fulfillment of the theme of the appointed time that prevented his capture earlier.
Jesus prays to the Father and says that the hour has come, marking the transition from the period when no one could seize him to the moment where he voluntarily gives himself up.
Here we see the end of the period during which Jesus was protected by his hour; he is handed over to death, which became inevitable now that the hour had arrived.
The psalm expresses a similar motif where God keeps his hand over the righteous so that enemies cannot seize him until God's time has come.
